  <h1 class="title">Research Knowledge Graph</h1>
  <p class="dek">A personal, plugin-first knowledge graph for academic research &mdash; not owned by any single vendor.</p>

  <h2 class="h2">Why</h2>
  <p>Every research tool I've used &mdash; reference managers, note apps, AI assistants &mdash; wants to own the graph. I wanted the graph to outlast all of them.</p>

  <h2 class="h2">How it works</h2>
  <p>The core defines capability contracts &mdash; a Research Library Connector, a Knowledge Store, a Scholarly Metadata Provider &mdash; and never talks to a specific product. Plugins implement the contracts. Swap a vendor, keep the graph.</p>

  <h2 class="h2">What I learned</h2>
  <p>Still in design &mdash; nothing shipped yet. The hard part isn't the graph itself, it's writing contracts stable enough that a plugin written in year one still works in year five.</p>

  <h2 class="h2">Code</h2>
  <p class="mono-link"><a href="https://github.com/alexanderwiebe/research-knowledge-graph">github.com/alexanderwiebe/research-knowledge-graph</a></p>
</div>
